no hype. Use only the provided material; every number must appear in it. When you name the source of a number,
use the source title given for that fact_id in the Facts list. State uncertainty honestly.

{"headline": "STABILITY trial of darapladib failed to reduce MACE in stable coronary heart disease (HR 0.94, p=0.199), consistent with a non-causal Lp-PLA2 target.",
"summary": "The STABILITY trial randomized 15,828 patients with stable coronary heart disease to darapladib or placebo, targeting a 15.5% relative risk reduction with 90% power and 1,500 planned primary endpoint events over a median 3.51 years follow-up. The trial did not meet its primary endpoint of cardiovascular death, nonfatal MI, or nonfatal stroke (HR 0.94, p=0.199). Darapladib achieved robust target engagement, inhibiting Lp-PLA2 activity by 49–67% in phase 2 studies, but the PLA2G7 genetic association score is 0.0 with no human genetic support for causality. The calculator predicted HR 1.0 (causal RRR 0%) based on non-causal target genetics. Two large phase 3 trials (STABILITY and SOLID-TIMI 52) both failed, safety was reassuring with no major SAE imbalance and lower hs-cTnI elevations on treatment. The evidence strongly supports target_not_causal and biomarker_not_causal as the primary failure categories with high confidence.",

  "15,828 participants randomized (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00799903 STABILITY)",
  "Primary endpoint: composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke (Study design and rationale for the Stabilization of pLaques usIng Darapladib-Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (SOLID-TIMI 52) trial in patients after an acute coronary syndrome)",
  "1,500 planned primary end point events with 90% power (Study design and rationale for the clinical outcomes of the STABILITY Trial (STabilization of Atherosclerotic plaque By Initiation of darapLadIb TherapY) comparing darapladib versus placebo in patients with coronary heart disease)",
  "Assumed 15.5% relative risk reduction (Study design and rationale for the clinical outcomes of the STABILITY Trial (STabilization of Atherosclerotic plaque By Initiation of darapLadIb TherapY) comparing darapladib versus placebo in patients with coronary heart disease)",
  "Median follow-up 3.51 years (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00799903 STABILITY)",
  "Observed HR 0.94, p=0.199 (GSK announces top-line results from pivotal Phase III study of darapladib in chronic coronary heart disease (12 November 2013))",
  "Readout: \"Study did not meet the primary endpoint measure\" (GSK announces top-line results from pivotal Phase III study of darapladib in chronic coronary heart disease (12 November 2013))",
  "Lp-PLA2 inhibition 49–67% in phase 2 (Effect of darapladib on plasma lipoprotein-associated phospholipase A2 activity in Japanese dyslipidemic patients, with exploratory analysis of a PLA2G7 gene polymorphism of Val279Phe.; Effects of the direct lipoprotein-associated phospholipase A(2) inhibitor darapladib on human coronary atherosclerotic plaque.)",
  "PLA2G7 genetic association score 0.0 (opentargets:PLA2G7)",
  "Calculator expected HR 1.0, causal RRR 0.0%, category target_not_causal (calculator)",
  "No major imbalance in serious adverse events (GSK announces top-line results from pivotal Phase III study of darapladib in chronic coronary heart disease (12 November 2013))",
  "hs-cTnI increases less frequent with darapladib: OR 0.53 overall, OR 0.219 in ACS subgroup (Darapladib effect on circulating high sensitive troponin in patients with acute coronary syndromes.)"

"what_would_change_this": "Only definitive human genetic evidence linking PLA2G7 loss-of-function to reduced coronary events could revive the target; current genetic score of 0.0 and two large outcome trial failures make this highly unlikely.",
"readthrough_note": "The SOLID-TIMI 52 trial in recent ACS patients (n≈13,000) also failed with darapladib, confirming failure across distinct high-risk populations. No other Lp-PLA2 inhibitor programmes are known to be active in cardiovascular outcomes."}
